weights.csoNote: Sepsis is the common endpoint of many of the infections below — treat the syndrome (cultures + early antibiotics + resuscitation) while seeking the source.
weights.weightCitation: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (current) + Sepsis-3 definitions (Singer M et al., JAMA 2016); qSOFA/NEWS2 for recognition

weights.csoNote: Kept UNCONDITIONAL must-not-miss (no pinWhen): malaria is holoendemic in Uganda, so 'test every fever' (RDT/microscopy) is the safe default and it should pin for everyone — unlike a Western/traveller setting where it would be exposure-conditional. A negative score/clinical impression does NOT exclude malaria. basePrior 4 = the single dominant fever cause in Uganda. Severe-malaria features (cerebral/coma, jaundice, severe anaemia, AKI, acidosis) escalate to emergency.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria (2025); Uganda National Malaria Control Programme / Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: cryptococcal meningitis common in advanced HIV (CD4<100); also TB and bacterial meningitis. Do not delay LP / empirical antibiotics; non-blanching rash suggests meningococcaemia.
weights.weightCitation: WHO meningitis guidance; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: disseminated/extrapulmonary TB is a leading cause of prolonged fever (PUO), especially in HIV; WHO four-symptom screen (cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss) applies.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB (2021); Uganda National TB & Leprosy Programme; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: rheumatic heart disease is the dominant predisposing lesion (vs degenerative/prosthetic in the West). Prolonged fever + a new/changing murmur should always prompt IE consideration (modified Duke criteria, blood cultures, echo).
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2023 Infective Endocarditis Guidelines (Delgado V et al., Eur Heart J 2023;44:3948-4042) — modified Duke criteria; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Loin pain + fever + rigors suggests pyelonephritis/urosepsis (vs lower UTI).
Uganda: in HIV consider bacterial pneumonia, PCP and TB in the same differential.
weights.weightCitation: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; WHO; Davidson's 24th ed; BTS CAP guideline

weights.csoNote: Very common in Uganda (faecal-oral, contaminated water/food); basePrior high but study-dependent. Classic pattern is SUSTAINED/stepwise fever with RELATIVE BRADYCARDIA and rose spots — neither is in the capture token set (gap). Watch for ILEAL PERFORATION (acute surgical abdomen).
weights.weightCitation: WHO typhoid/enteric fever guidance; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Crump JA & Mintz ED (enteric fever epidemiology); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.dx: Acute HIV seroconversion / acute retroviral syndrome
weights.csoNote: Frequently MISSED — a mononucleosis-like illness (fever + maculopapular rash + pharyngitis + generalised lymphadenopathy). HIV testing should be near-universal in a Ugandan fever workup. The antibody test may be NEGATIVE in the window (needs 4th-gen Ag/Ab + HIV RNA); the specific recent-HIV-exposure history is captured only loosely by 'high-risk exposure'.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Consolidated HIV Guidelines; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed (acute retroviral syndrome)

weights.csoNote: Uganda: amoebic liver abscess (Entamoeba histolytica) is a notable cause — RUQ pain + tender hepatomegaly + fever, male-predominant; pyogenic from a biliary/portal source. Right-sided pleuritic pain/shoulder-tip can occur.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; Harrison's 21st ed (amoebic & pyogenic liver abscess)

weights.csoNote: TIME-SENSITIVE — REVIEW AS THE OUTBREAK EVOLVES (retire/adjust when status changes). Sourced against a WHO-declared PHEIC (17 May 2026) Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak with confirmed cases in Kampala & Wakiso (Mulago catchment) as of June 2026. Early VHF is clinically INDISTINGUISHABLE from malaria/typhoid, so the CONDITIONAL pin fires on epidemiological risk within 21 days (contact with a suspected/confirmed case alive or dead, travel from an affected area, funeral exposure, or healthcare/IPC breach). A suspected case = ISOLATE + NOTIFY immediately, NOT routine workup. CAPTURE GAPS: (1) no bleeding/haemorrhage symptom token; (2) 'high-risk exposure' is too generic — add specific VHF-exposure capture; (3) this weighting is time-sensitive to outbreak status.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Disease Outbreak News — Ebola disease (Bundibugyo virus), DRC & Uganda (PHEIC 17 May 2026); CDC HAN00530; ECDC/Africa CDC guidance; Uganda MoH VHF case management; WHO/CDC VHF case definition (compatible symptoms + epidemiological risk within 21 days)

weights.csoNote: Under-diagnosed; basePrior uncertain but relevant in Uganda's cattle corridor / pastoralist communities. Hallmark is UNDULANT (fluctuating/relapsing) fever with arthralgia/SACROILIITIS and night sweats. Key exposures — livestock contact and UNPASTEURISED DAIRY — are not specifically tokenised ('high-risk exposure' is the only proxy); recommend an animal/dairy-exposure token.
weights.weightCitation: WHO brucellosis guidance; Davidson's 24th ed (undulant fever, sacroiliitis; unpasteurised dairy/livestock — Uganda cattle corridor)

weights.csoNote: Two distinct entities grouped per the brief. Rickettsioses (African tick-bite fever, R. africae) = fever + ESCHAR + regional lymphadenopathy + rash; relapsing fever (Borrelia, louse-/tick-borne) = RECURRING febrile episodes. Capture gaps: no 'eschar' token, and tick-bite/louse-crowding exposures map only loosely to 'high-risk exposure'. Rash overlaps many fever causes, so weight is supportive not decisive.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed (African tick-bite fever R. africae — eschar/rash; louse-borne B. recurrentis & tick-borne B. duttonii relapsing fever, East Africa)

weights.csoNote: Under-diagnosed; basePrior uncertain. Severe form (Weil's) = fever + JAUNDICE + AKI + haemorrhage, with severe MYALGIA (esp. calves) and CONJUNCTIVAL SUFFUSION. Capture gaps: myalgia/calf-tenderness, conjunctival suffusion and AKI aren't well tokenised; the freshwater/floodwater/rodent-urine exposure maps only to 'high-risk exposure'. The fever+jaundice+AKI triad overlaps malaria and viral hepatitis.
weights.weightCitation: WHO leptospirosis guidance; Davidson's 24th ed (Weil's disease — fever, jaundice, AKI; freshwater/rodent/flood exposure)

weights.csoNote: DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION — must not anchor here before malaria and serious/treatable bacterial causes are excluded. Included as the honest common-benign anchor (most acute fever self-resolves) and to hold a slot for arboviral illness (dengue/chikungunya) where epidemiologically relevant. basePrior setting-dependent (lower at a referral hospital).
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed (self-limiting viral febrile illness; arboviral — dengue/chikungunya — where relevant); diagnosis of exclusion
